  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

Earlier this year, we launched ElevenLabs for Government, and are now looking for an exceptional product marketer to help us scale this story into global government and public sector markets.

Government agencies everywhere are being asked to answer more calls, in more languages, with the same amount or less staff. ElevenAgents resolves support, cuts hold times, and reaches people who cannot navigate a website or sit on a phone line. This role is to help us shape these capabilities into every market where governments serve citizens by voice.

  • Own positioning and packaging for ElevenLabs for Government

  • Scale the narrative across regions: National and Local government in the UK, EU, Federal, State and Local in the US, and public sector agencies across APAC, LATAM, and more

  • Anchor everything in citizen outcomes: non-emergency contact centers (311), benefits and eligibility, health and social services, licensing and permitting, and more

  • Position our solution for accessibility, compliance, language requirements, and the security and data residency mandates

  • Lead industry content, landing pages, and thought leadership pieces

  • You are an experienced product marketer who has scaled messaging into Government and Public Sector segments, from a growth or product marketing seat, ideally both

  • You've sold or marketed into more than one segment of public sector

  • Technical enough to become our internal expert on conversational agents: latency, telephony, tool calls, evals, and guardrails

  • Excellent project management across multiple countries, regulatory regimes, and simultaneous launches

  • You take initiative and work autonomously from day one, prioritizing learning and contribution while leaving ego aside

ElevenLabs spends meaningfully on paid acquisition, and that spend is only as good as the data behind it. We are looking for an engineer to own our measurement layer end to end: the tag manager setup, the tracking and attribution scripts on our sites, and the server-to-server conversion tracking that feeds our ad platforms.

Day to day you will work closely with the paid marketing team: fixing tracking bugs as they come in, setting up tracking for new landing pages and campaigns, and debugging discrepancies between platform-reported conversions and our internal data. Longer term, you will define how tracking should properly work here and build the monitoring so we catch breakage in hours, not weeks.

This role sits between frontend engineering, data engineering, and marketing. You will add and improve tracking scripts without hurting pagespeed, keep our server-side GTM container healthy, make sure consent and regional restrictions are correctly enforced, and ensure the right channels get credit for the right conversions. Your work directly decides how a large paid budget gets allocated.

What you will do

  • Own our tag manager setup end to end, including the server-side GTM container, and review any changes other teams want to make

  • Work with the paid marketing team daily: fix tracking bugs, set up tracking for new landing pages and campaigns, and debug discrepancies between platform-reported conversions and our internal data

  • Build and maintain server-to-server conversion tracking (Meta CAPI, Google Enhanced Conversions, and similar) and validate pixel vs server deduplication

  • Improve tracking script performance and correctness, keeping script impact on pagespeed and Core Web Vitals within budget

  • Make sure consent handling and regional restrictions are correctly enforced across markets

  • Define event schema and UTM conventions, and document them so tracking for new campaigns is correct by default

  • Build monitoring and alerting for the measurement stack so we catch broken tracking within hours, not weeks

  • Review PRs that add conversion events to the main app, and work with product engineering on tracking integrations

Requirements

  • Strong JavaScript/TypeScript, comfortable working in both frontend code and a production application codebase

  • Hands-on experience with Google Tag Manager, including server-side GTM, and at least one conversion API (Meta CAPI, Google Enhanced Conversions, or similar) implemented server-to-server

  • Experience debugging attribution discrepancies end to end: pixel vs server deduplication, UTM conventions, event schema design

  • Solid understanding of web performance and how to add tracking without degrading Core Web Vitals

  • Working knowledge of consent and privacy requirements (Consent Mode v2, regional restrictions) and SQL for validating tracking data in the warehouse

Bonus

  • CDP experience (Segment, RudderStack, Snowplow)

  • Product analytics tools (GA4, Amplitude, PostHog) and dbt

  • Next.js experience

  • Exposure to incrementality testing or media mix modelling

Growth potential

We believe in hiring the best talent in the world to make an impact in the right role at the right time. At ElevenLabs, strong performance creates opportunities for growth. Here are some of the career paths you can expect after excelling in this role:

  • Own the whole martech and measurement area as it grows, potentially leading a small marketing engineering team

  • Grow toward senior/staff IC on the engineering track

  • Broaden into data engineering and attribution modelling, or into growth engineering more widely (experimentation, landing page infrastructure)

Location

This role is remote and can be executed globally. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in London, New York, Madrid, Warsaw and many more.

title: Senior Product Manager (Data API)
description:
About 9fin

9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets — the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion.

Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets.

Today, 9fin powers teams at 300+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms, and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption.

We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide.

The Opportunity

 

9fin has built one of the most comprehensive datasets in credit and debt markets: news, financials, cap tables, instrument data, legal documents, and ESG analysis. Today, most clients access that data through 9fin.com. But a large and growing segment of the market wants to consume our data programmatically to power firm-level workflows at scale: a negative news signal triggers an automated credit review, updated financials trigger a portfolio rebalance, a covenant keyword triggers a sanctions flag.

 

These buyers (quant desks, data engineering teams, systematic investors, risk and compliance functions) will never log into a web application. They need APIs, data feeds, and cloud-native delivery through platforms like Snowflake. At comparable financial data providers, this distribution channel represents 20-30% of total revenue. 9fin is at the beginning of this journey.

 

The challenge is to turn 9fin's integrated dataset into a portfolio of standalone data products with a coherent commercial strategy. You will define how the data gets packaged (what goes together, what stands alone, how it's tiered and priced), the order in which products go to market, and the commercial models that fit each buyer segment: quant desks, data engineering teams, risk and compliance functions, and systematic investors. You will work in lockstep with the Head of Pre-Sales, who owns technical validation and deal execution, to ensure that what you build maps to how these buyers actually evaluate and procure data. The first candidates pan news content, financials and cap tables, instrument data, and legal data (complex, high-value, and genuinely unsolved at the data representation layer).

 

You will work cross-functionally across our platform teams, analytics engineering, and the domain squads that own the underlying datasets. You will also work closely with Sales to support a fundamentally different GTM motion: solution-selling with partner clients, joint POCs, multi-stakeholder deals, and usage-based commercial models rather than seat-based subscriptions.

 

This is a 0-to-1 build. If you have built API or data products before and want to do it again in a market where the opportunity is wide open, this is it.

 
 

What You'll Do

 

Product Strategy & Execution

  • Define the product vision and strategy for 9fin's external data distribution: APIs, data shares, and future delivery mechanisms (cloud sync, pub/sub).

  • Own the data catalogue decisions: which datasets to expose, in what format, through which channels, and in what order, balancing client demand, data readiness, and commercial potential

  • Design the developer experience end-to-end: API design, documentation, developer portal, sandbox/playground, error handling, rate limiting, and versioning

  • Work with analytics engineering and domain teams to define schemas, data models, and transformation logic that make 9fin's data consumable and valuable outside the application

  • Use a partner model to validate early: select and work closely with 1-2 clients during development to co-develop and prove out each data product before broader launch

  • Shape the commercial model for API products: packaging, tiering, usage-based pricing, distribution controls, and entitlement structures that capture the value of programmatic data access

 

Data Quality, Infrastructure & Compliance

 

  • Partner with the Head of Analytics to ensure data products meet the reliability, freshness, and accuracy standards that enterprise clients building automated systems expect

  • Define SLAs for data delivery (latency, uptime, completeness) and build the monitoring and metering infrastructure to back them up

  • Own the entitlements and access control layer: ensuring the right clients can access the right data under the right contractual terms, with appropriate usage limits and controls

  • Work with Legal to define data usage policies, including restrictions on redistribution, AI training and model embedding, and onward use, protecting 9fin's data IP while enabling legitimate client workflows

  • Establish feedback loops between API consumers and domain teams so that usage patterns and client requests improve the underlying data over time

 

Cross-Functional Leadership & GTM

 

  • Coordinate across platform engineering, analytics engineering, domain squads, and the Head of Analytics to align priorities and ship a cohesive product without a dedicated squad

  • Influence teams you do not manage; build relationships that make cross-functional delivery work despite competing priorities

  • Support the shift to a solution-selling GTM motion: work with Sales and Customer Success on partner selection, POC design, technical onboarding, and commercial structuring for API deals

  • Engage directly with enterprise clients and their technical teams during pilots and integrations; this is a client-facing role, not a back-office one

  • Communicate strategy, progress, and trade-offs transparently to leadership, engineering, and commercial teams

  • Translate technical API and data infrastructure concepts into language that non-technical stakeholders (Sales, Legal, Finance) can act on

 

What We're Looking For

 

  • 5+ years of product management experience, with at least 2 years building API products, data platforms, or data distribution products at a B2B company

  • Experience designing APIs for external consumers: you have opinions on schema design, versioning strategies, rate limiting, and what makes developer documentation actually useful

  • Track record of shipping data products where you managed the full lifecycle: from defining what data to expose, through schema design, to commercial packaging and client onboarding

  • Understanding of data infrastructure concepts: data pipelines, warehouses, ETL/ELT, data modelling, and platforms like Snowflake

  • Comfortable with SQL and Python and capable of interrogating data to validate quality, understand usage patterns, and inform product decisions

  • Experience working in a solution-selling or partner-led GTM model: you have been involved in POCs, pilots, or co-development with enterprise clients, not just self-serve product launches

  • Proven ability to lead cross-functionally without a dedicated team: you coordinate across engineering, data, and commercial functions through influence, not authority

  • Strong commercial instinct: you understand how enterprise data buyers evaluate providers, and you can shape a product that competes on data quality, coverage, and ease of integration

  • Clear communicator who can translate between technical and commercial audiences

 

Nice to Have

  • Familiarity with credit markets, debt instruments, or how buy-side/sell-side firms consume financial data

  • Experience with Snowflake data sharing, marketplace listings, or similar cloud data distribution mechanisms

  • Experience building entitlements, licensing, or access control systems for data products

  • Understanding of data licensing, redistribution terms, or AI usage policies in the context of enterprise data products

 

Benefits

 

  • Competitive, market-benchmarked salary

  • Pension with 7% company matching

  • Private medical insurance, paid sick leave, income protection, group life assurance

  • Season ticket and cycle-to-work schemes

  • Hybrid flexibility with up to 3 months annual work abroad

  • 25 holiday days plus local public holidays (exchangeable)

  • One-month paid sabbatical after 5 years; enhanced parental leave

  • Professional development budget and regular social events

Since 2012, we've revolutionised how these businesses access finance, turning what was once a lengthy, frustrating process into something remarkable: funding that's fast, flexible, and actually works for modern businesses.

Our impact speaks for itself: we've provided billions in funding to over 150,000 businesses across Europe, making us one of the continent's leading fintech innovators. But we're just getting started. Our mission? To empower one million businesses with the financial tools they deserve.

We combine cutting-edge technology and data science with genuine human understanding to make finance feel less like a barrier and more like a superpower. Whether it's managing cash flow or seizing unexpected opportunities, we ensure businesses get the funds they need – often within minutes.

The team

The Repeats team is one of iwoca's funnel teams. We grow customer lifetime value after a business's first loan. That means we own the underwriting, pricing, and product experience for two segments that make up most of iwoca's back-book value: top-up customers who borrow again while still repaying, and loan-ended customers who return for a new loan. Almost every repeat borrower goes through code we own. The team is cross-functional – backend, frontend, product, design, data science and analytics – shipping behind split tests and measuring impact in Looker rather than on gut feel.

The role

Your first project will be the re-architecture of our flex-loan repeat offer pipeline: the flow that decides who is eligible for a new loan, what they pay, and how much they can borrow. This area has been under-invested for years. Once the new pipeline is in place, product has a clear runway of features ready to ship on top of it.

  • Help monitor production and troubleshoot issues when they come up.

  • Show up to team rituals – stand-ups, retros, planning – with context and questions.

  • Write clean, well-tested Python, and take part in code reviews to learn from teammates and keep quality high.

  • Pick up front-end work in Pandora (React, TypeScript) so you can own features end-to-end over time.

  • You use AI (Cursor, Claude Code or similar) in your daily flow – whether for work or for fun. You use it to blast through boilerplate and research so you can focus on the hard parts: complex architecture, rigour and high-stakes decisions.

title: Procurement and Payments Manager
description:
The opportunity:

This is an exciting opportunity to join the Girls' Learning Trust at a pivotal stage in our development. Following significant investment in our finance systems, processes and team structure, and with a fourth school joining the Trust in November, we are continuing to strengthen our Shared Professional Services to support a growing and ambitious organisation.

As Procurement & Payments Manager, you will lead a newly developed function responsible for procurement, supplier and contract management, payment processes and associated financial controls across all Trust schools and Shared Professional Services. Reporting directly to the Chief Financial Officer, you will lead and develop a small team whilst working closely with budget holders and senior leaders across the Trust.

This role offers a unique opportunity to make a tangible impact. In addition to ensuring the effective operation of procurement and payment processes, you will play a key role in helping the Trust achieve greater value for money through improved procurement practices, stronger supplier management, more effective contract oversight and the identification of efficiencies across our non-staff expenditure.

What we offer:

Staff are our most valued asset, and we are continuously working to introduce initiatives or make changes which support them both professionally and personally. Some of the initiatives we have recently introduced are a new Health and Wellbeing Cash plan for staff and their dependents; a generous discretionary leave scheme; and we have made changes to the performance review process ensuring a strong focus on continued professional development.

Our commitment to you:

You will have the opportunity to shape and develop an important Trust-wide function, lead a committed team and contribute to the continued growth and success of the organisation. Most importantly, your work will help ensure that every pound spent delivers the greatest possible benefit to our schools and the young people they serve.

We recognise that your induction and training will be key to your success and we will invest time to ensure you are given all the guidance and support needed at the outset and over the ensuing weeks to fulfil your role effectively.

We will uphold a culture that promotes kindness, collaboration and recognition, ensuring an open, safe, supportive and inclusive environment where everyone feels heard, valued and empowered to contribute.

Key responsibilities for the role include:

Leading the Trust's Procurement and Payments function across all schools and Shared Professional Services, ensuring the effective management of procurement, supplier relationships, contract administration, payment processes and associated financial controls.

Leading and developing a small team, working collaboratively with budget holders and senior leaders, and supporting the delivery of value for money across the Trust's non-staff expenditure.

Ensuring procurement and payment activities are carried out efficiently, compliantly and in accordance with Trust financial regulations, whilst fostering a culture of proactive procurement planning and continuous improvement.

The successful candidate will:

We are looking for an individual who enjoys combining strong financial controls with a commercial mindset. You will be equally comfortable supporting colleagues, challenging existing ways of working, analysing expenditure and identifying opportunities to improve services and reduce costs.

The successful candidate will be someone who can build strong relationships, influence stakeholders and help foster a culture of proactive procurement planning across the Trust.

Key Application Dates:

  • Shortlisting Date: Monday 7 September
  • First Stage Interview Date (online): Wednesday 16 September
  • Second Stage Interview Date (in person): Tuesday 22 September
  • Start Date: ASAP

Safer recruitment:

The Girls’ Learning Trust is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff to share this commitment. In order to meet this responsibility, we follow a rigorous selection process to discourage and screen out unsuitable applicants.

As well as verification of identity, we ask all employees to undertake an enhanced DBS disclosure. In line with Keeping Children Safe in Education (KCSIE) guidance, we may also conduct an online search about any shortlisted candidates as part of our due diligence to identify any matters that might relate directly to our legal duty to meet safeguarding duties in accordance with Keeping Children Safe in Education (KCSIE)

We welcome applications from all suitably qualified people and aim to employ a culturally diverse workforce, which reflects the nature of our communities.

title: Senior Growth Software Engineer
location: Flexible / Remote, London, United Kingdom, Oslo, Norway
description:
Job Requisition ID #

25WD92032

About the Role

We are searching for a strong Growth-focused Software Engineer to our Product Growth team driving user product adoption, engagement and monetisation for our next-generation, AI-powered architecture design product, Forma.

In this role, you will sit at the critical intersection of engineering, product, and business strategy. We operate with a strong commercial bias: we believe that code is a means to an end. Your true measure of success will be the tangible commercial outcomes and user growth you drive. If you are passionate about moving the needle on key business metrics, running rapid experiments, and focusing relentlessly on the end result, this is the perfect role for you.

Responsibilities

  • Drive growth: You will design, build, and deploy experiments aimed at improving user adoption and engagement as well as our early self-serve monetisation experiments.
  • Execute rapid experimentation: Formulate hypotheses and execute A/B tests at a high velocity. You will build minimum viable features to validate ideas quickly, understanding that many tests will fail, and that this failure is a celebrated and necessary part of the discovery process.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally: Work seamlessly with Product Managers, Designers, Data Analysts and Marketing to identify growth bottlenecks and brainstorm innovative, high-impact solutions.
  • Make data-driven decisions: Analyze experiment results and user data to uncover hidden insights. You will constantly ask "Why?" to understand user behaviour and inform your next set of technical and product decisions.
  • Practice pragmatic engineering: Make smart trade-offs between engineering perfection and speed to market. You will handle edge cases pragmatically, often finding creative solutions that require minimal engineering effort to validate a concept.
  • Leverage AI to multiply output: Act as an AI-accelerated generalist. You will use modern AI tools to accelerate your workflow, stepping outside traditional engineering boundaries to assist with lightweight product management, data analysis and maybe even design tasks to get experiments live faster.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for someone who embodies specific traits that align with our outcome-over-code philosophy. Prior experience in a formal Growth Engineering role is highly desirable, a relentless growth mindset is the absolute prerequisite.

  • Growth mindset & commercial bias: You care deeply about the business impact of your work. You understand that engineering is a tool to solve user problems and drive revenue. And you have a demonstrated ability to drive the team's work to completion, breaking complex tasks into smaller, actionable pieces.
  • AI-accelerated generalist: You have a strong bias toward using AI to multiply your output. You are comfortable stepping outside traditional engineering boundaries, using AI tools to assist with lightweight product management and design tasks to get experiments live faster.
  • Self-starter with infinite curiosity: You are proactive about coming up with your own hypotheses and experiments. You do not wait to be handed a rigid roadmap; you find opportunities in the data and act on them.
  • Resilient to lost code: You are completely comfortable with the reality of experimentation. You know that a significant portion of the code you write will be discarded if an experiment does not yield the desired results, and you do not let ego get in the way of progress.
  • Comfortable with unscalable solutions: You understand that early tests might be small, scrappy, and unpolished. You prefer a pragmatic approach to validate an idea in days over spending weeks building a highly scalable but unproven feature.
  • Product-minded communicator: You possess strong product instincts and can articulate the "why" behind your technical choices to non-technical stakeholders. You thrive in an autonomous culture and enable co-workers through knowledge sharing.
  • Code all-rounder: Experience with multiple languages and technologies, including modern frontend frameworks, large-scale systems, and cloud computing.

Qualifications

  • Experience with data-driven development, A/B testing methodologies, and iterating based on user behavior data.
  • Interest in conversion optimization, user journey analysis, and driving impact aligned with our mission.
  • Experience across modern frontend frameworks, large-scale systems, and cloud computing.
  • Comfort using modern AI tools to accelerate workflow across engineering, product, and design tasks.

Even if you feel you don't check off all the items on the list, we still encourage you to apply.

Welcome to Autodesk! Amazing things are created every day with our software - from the greenest buildings and cleanest cars to the smartest factories and biggest hit movies. We help innovators turn their ideas into reality, transforming not only how things are made, but what can be made.

title: Finance Apprentice
description:
Finance Apprentice (based at Woodford Primary School) - Join the WeST Family

Westcountry Schools Trust (WeST) is a tight-knit family of 31 schools - 8 secondary and 23 primaries - working together across the Southwest. We are ambitious for every child and committed to delivering excellence through collaboration, innovation, and shared values.

We are seeking a motivated and organised Finance Apprentice to join our finance team based at Woodford Primary School. The post is offered on a permanent basis. However, the role is designed around the completion of a finance apprenticeship pathway and candidates will be expected to fully engage with and successfully complete the required training and qualifications to progress within the position. This is an exciting opportunity for someone who is looking to begin or develop a career in finance while gaining practical experience across a busy and supportive Trust environment. The role will support specific WeST schools and the Trust as a whole, working within the Academy Trust Handbook and WeST Financial Procedures and Regulations to help ensure deadlines, audit requirements and financial processes are met.

About This Role

As Finance Apprentice, you will work as part of the finance team, providing comprehensive administrative and finance support to the Finance Team, School Business Accountant and Senior Procurement and Contracts Officer where required. You will develop relevant skills and expertise as the work and responsibilities of the post grow, enabling you to play an active role and contribute effectively to the wider team.

This role will include supporting a range of finance processes such as maintaining records for payment systems, processing invoices, supporting banking and reconciliations, assisting with financial reports and records, maintaining financial systems, supporting audit activity, helping with procurement and contracts processes, processing expenses and assisting with sales ledger and debt management activity.

You will also work towards successfully completing an AAT Level 3 Apprenticeship, gaining valuable knowledge and practical experience within a school trust finance setting.

What We’re Looking For

We’re seeking someone who is:

  • Keen to develop a career in finance and committed to successfully completing an AAT Level 3 Apprenticeship.
  • Organised, methodical and able to prioritise tasks to meet deadlines.
  • Able to work accurately and maintain confidentiality at all times.
  • A confident communicator with good verbal and written communication skills.
  • Self-motivated, able to use initiative and work effectively as part of a team.
  • Computer literate, with a working knowledge of Microsoft Office.
  • Committed to safeguarding, KCSIE and supporting Trust policies, including Safeguarding, Health and Safety, Equality and Diversity.
  • Aligned with WeST’s values of collaboration, aspiration, integrity, compassion and respect.

Whilst the indicative working pattern is full time, all year round, we are happy to discuss flexible working.

Please note that this vacancy may close early if we identify and appoint a suitable candidate before the advertised closing date, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Procedures

All appointments are subject to pre-employment checks. That means:

  • We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expect all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. A copy of our Child Protection Policy & Safeguarding Policy is attached.
  • Your identity will be confirmed by sight of original, official documents such as a Birth Certificate, Passport etc. in line with the Asylum and Immigration Act 1996.
  • Original documents relating to all the qualifications you have listed on your application form must be supplied.
  • Your employment history will be thoroughly examined and clarification will be sought where there are gaps or other discrepancies arising from information provided either by you as the candidate or your referee.
  • References will be used to check dates of employment and your relevant experience. A minimum of two written references will be taken up and these references will be requested before the interview.
  • References should cover the last 3-5 years’ work history, as a minimum.
  • An online search of shortlisted candidates will be conducted in accordance with Part Three ‘Safer Recruitment’ of Keeping Children Safe in Education statutory guidance.
  • The identity of referees and information relating to disclosures will be verified.
  • You will be required to provide details of any relevant unspent or spent convictions in accordance with the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (Exceptions) (Amendment) Order 1986.
  • An enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check will be requested. Please note that it is an offence to apply, offer or accept to do any work with children (paid or unpaid) if disqualified from working with children. Applicants will be challenged where inconsistencies exist. Please be aware that a firm offer of appointment will only be made after receipt and verification of all satisfactory checks. Westcountry Schools Trust will carry out these checks and should you fail these checks, our offer of employment will be withdrawn.

Further details about the Trust can be found on our website (www.westst.org.uk) and on My New Term (https://mynewterm.com/trust/Westcountry-Schools-Trust/142688)

description:
PREMISES AND COMPLIANCE MANAGER

Salary: NJC Scale SO1, Point 23 to 25 (£34,434 to £36,363 per annum FTE). Starting salary £34,434 per annum on point 23.

Contract: Permanent. 37 hours per week, Monday to Friday. 52 weeks per year

Start date: As soon as possible

Place of work: : St Peters School, Huntingdon

Place of wor

St Peter's School is seeking to appoint a proactive, organised and highly motivated Premises & Compliance Manager to play a key role in ensuring our school environment is safe, secure, compliant and well-maintained for all students, staff and visitors. This is an exciting opportunity for an individual with strong organisational skills, a sound knowledge of health and safety and compliance requirements, and a commitment to supporting the effective operation of a busy secondary school.

As Premises & Compliance Manager, you will take responsibility for the coordination and completion of statutory compliance activities across the school, including risk assessments, compliance testing, contractor management and the monitoring of remedial actions. You will ensure that essential maintenance records, compliance registers and site documentation are maintained accurately and that the school continues to meet all relevant legislative and regulatory requirements.

You will lead on compliance processes, coordinate maintenance and contractor activities, monitor utilities and contracts, and contribute to the effective management of the school site and facilities. You will also play an important role in ensuring the school remains operationally ready each day and support the planning and delivery of site improvement projects.

The successful candidate will have experience in premises, facilities, estates or compliance management and possess a strong understanding of health and safety legislation. You will be highly organised, able to manage competing priorities effectively, and confident in working with a wide range of stakeholders. Excellent administrative, communication and problem-solving skills are essential, together with a proactive and flexible approach to supporting the school's operational needs.

This is an excellent opportunity to make a significant contribution to the continued success of St Peter's School. The role offers a varied workload, professional responsibility and the opportunity to help shape and maintain an environment where students can learn and thrive in safe, compliant and well-maintained surroundings.

By joining The CAM Academy Trust, you will have the opportunity to collaborate, share expertise and develop best practice across a family of schools committed to delivering excellence for all young people. At St Peter's School, we are committed to investing in our staff and offer a wide range of professional development opportunities to support career growth and progression.

The CAM Academy Trust is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. Successful applicants will be subject to all necessary pre-employment checks, including an enhanced DBS check.

For further details on our school please visit our website www.stpetershuntingdon.org

title: Staff Brand Designer
description:
Headquarters: Remote

 URL: https://webflow.com/

 Webflow is the agentic web marketing platform for modern marketing teams, helping organizations build, manage, and optimize high-performing web experiences that drive predictable growth and strengthen brand trust. Building at Webflow will need grit, because we move fast, without ever sacrificing craft or quality.

 We're looking for a Staff Brand Designer who works in the space between brand and web—someone who can hold a brand idea and build it themselves. Our marketing site is where most people meet Webflow, which makes it the primary surface of our brand rather than a place we put finished work. You'll design that experience and take it all the way into production on our own platform. The brand doesn't stop at the site, though—it shows up in campaigns, conference environments, film, and the product itself—and you'll work across those surfaces too. The border between those disciplines is disappearing in practice: a conference identity now ships as a motion system and a site in the same breath, and an announcement has to hold in a keynote and a viewport in the same week. This role also sits closest to the edge of what's newly possible, so we care most about someone who is already experimenting—putting AI and agentic tooling to real use and bringing back what holds up. You'll sit on Brand Studio, Webflow's in-house creative team, as a senior individual contributor working alongside brand designers, motion, and marketing partners.

 About the role:

• Location: Remote-first (United States; BC & ON, Canada)

• Full-time

• Permanent

• Exempt

• The cash compensation for this role is tailored to align with the cost of labor in different geographic markets. We've structured the base pay ranges for this role into zones for our geographic markets, and the specific base pay within the range will be determined by the candidate’s geographic location, job-related experience, knowledge, qualifications, and skills.

• United States (all figures cited below are in USD and pertain to workers in the United States)

• Zone A: $ 162,500 - $195,000

• Zone B: $ 153,300 - $184,000

• Zone C: $ 143,300 - $172,000

• Canada (figures cited below are in CAD and pertain to workers in ON & BC, Canada)

• 177,000 - 213,000

 This role is also eligible to participate in Webflow's company-wide bonus program. Target amounts are a percentage of base salary and vary by career level. Payouts are based on company performance against established financial and operational goals.

 Please visit our Careers page for more information on which locations are included in each of our geographic pay zones. However, please confirm the zone for your specific location with your recruiter.

• Application Information:

• Application deadline: applications accepted on an ongoing basis until position is closed and filled

• This posting is for an existing vacancy

• Reporting to the Manager, Brand Studio

 As a Staff Brand Designer, you'll…

 Design the web as our primary brand surface

• Treat webflow.com as the place most people meet the brand, and design it as an experience rather than a stack of sections.

• Shape pacing, narrative, and flow across a visitor's path, not just the layout of individual pages.

• Express the brand through behavior—type, motion, interaction, and state—not only through how a frame looks at rest.

• Extend the brand system into web-native patterns and components that other designers and marketers can use without you in the room.

 Work in the space between brand and web

• Design and build in the same motion, carrying work from brand idea to shipped page without handing it off at the seam.

• Act as the primary technical owner of Webflow's marketing surface area, from CMS architecture to component systems to publishing workflow.

• Build on Webflow as our most sophisticated customer, so the site stands as proof of what the platform can do rather than an exception to it.

• Hold the craft bar on brand expression and the technical bar on implementation at the same time, and know when the two are in tension.

• Make architectural calls that balance ambition against performance, scalability, and the cost of maintaining them a year from now.

• Ship launches, campaign pages, and fixes with speed and accuracy under real deadline pressure, including moments like Webflow Conf, and own performance, accessibility, and SEO health as ongoing commitments.

 Work across the brand's other surfaces

• Bring the same standard to work that isn't a website: campaign systems, conference environments, editorial, film, and the brand's expression inside the product.

• Design for coherence across surfaces, so an idea that starts on the site still holds up in a keynote, a video, or a physical space.

• Understand how a brand system has to behave differently in each medium, and help evolve the system itself rather than only its web expression.

 Experiment, and put what works into production

• Work in the open with AI-assisted design and development, generative code, and agentic build tooling, and bring back what actually holds up under a quality bar.

• Explore advanced and pre-release platform capabilities and ship them ahead of the market.

• Build the experiments that make an argument—a working prototype that settles a debate faster than a deck would.

• Use generative and agentic tooling where it closes the gap between designing a system and building it, which is increasingly the same act.

• Develop the team's practice as you go, so a tool you proved out this month is something everyone is using next month.

• Feed real practitioner insight back to Product and Engineering, because you're building on the thing we sell.

 Unblock the business

• Partner with Brand Studio, Product Marketing, Growth, Legal, and Events to get campaigns and launches live without compromising the site.

• Reduce dependency bottlenecks by making your expertise available early, when decisions are still cheap to change.

• Mentor designers and marketers through pairing, feedback, and the systems and guardrails you build for them.

• Translate technical constraints into plain language so non-technical partners can make good tradeoffs themselves.

 In addition to the responsibilities outlined above, at Webflow we will support you in identifying where your interests and development opportunities lie and we'll help you incorporate them into your role.

 About you:

 Requirements:

• BS/BA college degree or relevant experience

• 8+ years of experience spanning brand design and web design or development, with work that clearly shows both

• Demonstrated experience designing marketing websites as a primary surface of a brand—narrative, flow, and interaction across a journey, not just individual page layouts

• Deep, demonstrable Webflow expertise, including complex CMS structures, components, interactions, performance work, and system-level thinking

• Experience contributing to brand work beyond websites—campaigns, environments, editorial, motion, or product surfaces—with a view on how a brand system has to change shape in each

• Active AI fluency: you are already using AI and agentic tooling in real production work, and can show what you have built with it, what you have thrown away, and how you tell those apart

• Familiarity with code: you read HTML and CSS comfortably, can follow and adapt JavaScript, and are not stuck when a build needs to go past the visual editor. Professional development experience is not required.

• A portfolio that shows both identity-level craft and shipped, high-traffic sites you can speak to at the architecture level

 You’ll thrive as a Staff Brand Designer if you:

• Think about a website as an experience with pacing and narrative, rather than a set of pages to be laid out.

• Treat new tools as material to be tested rather than trends to have an opinion about, and can tell the difference between a capability and a demo.

• Move fluidly between a type-scale decision and a CMS schema decision, and consider neither beneath you nor outside your job.

• Are as interested in what the brand does in a room or a keynote as in what it does in a viewport.

• Like that the work is public evidence—people inspect how webflow.com is built to decide what the platform can do.

• Reach for a prototype before a deck, and would rather show the thing working than describe it.

• Think in systems first, and can explain why you structured something the way you did three releases later.

• Care about craft at the level of a 40ms transition and a 200-page class system in equal measure.

• Bring calm and clarity to complex, fast-moving launches, and would rather surface a risk early than absorb it quietly.

• Want meaningful technical ownership without formal people management, and get real satisfaction from scaling your impact through standards, tooling, and mentorship.

• Communicate well with people who don't share your vocabulary, and give feedback that makes work better rather than smaller.

• Have opinions about where the web is going as agents take on more of the building, and are already testing them in production.

• Stay curious and open to growth—demonstrating a proactive embrace of AI, and actively building and applying fluency in emerging technologies to elevate how we work, drive faster outcomes, and expand collective impact.

 Our Core Behaviors:

• Build lasting customer trust. We build trust by taking action that puts customer trust first.

• Win together. We play to win, and we win as one team. Success at Webflow isn't a solo act.

• Reinvent ourselves. We don't just improve what exists, we imagine what's possible.

• Own it all the way. We move fast because the moment demands it, and we hold ourselves accountable to deliver outcomes — for each other, and for customers.

 Benefits

• Ownership in what you help build. Every permanent Webflower receives equity (RSUs) in our growing, privately held company.

• Health coverage that actually covers you. Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans for full-time employees and their dependents, with Webflow covering most premiums.

• Support for every stage of family life . 12 weeks of paid parental leave for all parents and 6+ weeks of additional paid leave for birthing parents. Plus inclusive care for family planning, menopause, and midlife transitions.

• Time off that’s actually off. Flexible vacation, paid holidays, and a sabbatical program to help you recharge and come back inspired.

• Wellness for the whole you. Access to mental health resources, therapy and coaching.

• Invest in your future. A 401(k) with 100% employer match (up to $6,000/year) in the U.S., and support for retirement savings globally.

• Monthly stipends that flex with your life. Localized support for work and wellness expenses — from Wi-Fi to workouts.

• Bonus for building together. All full-time, permanent, non-commission employees are eligible for our annual WIN bonus program.

 Remote, together

 At Webflow, equality is a core tenet of our culture. We are an Equal Opportunity (EEO)/Veterans/Disabled Employer and are committed to building an inclusive global team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, beliefs, and experiences. Employment decisions are made on the basis of job-related criteria without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other classification protected by applicable law. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, Webflow will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

title: Customer Support Systems & Analytics Architect
description:
Headquarters: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States

 We’re looking for a Customer Support Systems & Analytics Architect to own the data strategy and reporting function within the Customer Support organisation at Mercury. As our operations grow in complexity—spanning multiple channels, an expanding BPO model, and sophisticated AI automation—we are moving away from fragmented, project-based data support toward a model of holistic ownership.

 In this role, you will be responsible for how we capture, structure, and connect data across our CS systems - including Zendesk and our AI Agent - to drive informed decision-making across the team. You will ensure our systems are configured in a way that produces reliable, high-quality data, and you will translate that data into actionable insights for CS leadership and stakeholders. You’ll sit at the intersection of data, operations, and customer experience, partnering closely with CS leadership, Strategy and Ops, and cross-functional teams like Data to make sure our reporting infrastructure is built to scale. Your work will be foundational to how the CS organisation measures performance, identifies opportunities, and drives decision-making.

 Key Responsibilities

• Unified reporting and analytics: Actively build and maintain reports and dashboards that give the CS organisation clear visibility into key performance metrics, trends, and performance across channels, teams and projects - from our internal Support team to our BPO partners.

• CS Systems configuration and data governance: Work closely with systems admins to advise on the structural setup of our Zendesk instance across customer-facing teams, ensuring it is configured to generate clean, consistent, and reliable data while maintaining secure systems and efficient workflows.

• Data hygiene standards: Define and enforce standards for how data is captured across CS systems so that reporting is accurate, trustworthy, and reproducible

• AI automation data oversight: Monitor and analyse data from our AI chatbot, ensuring it is tracked in a way that supports quality reviews and decision-making across the CS organisation

• Insights to action: Translate raw data and reporting into clear recommendations that help CS leadership make decisions on resourcing, tooling, process improvements, and strategy

• Stakeholder support: Partner with cross-functional partners in areas like Product, Data and Strategic Finance to understand their data needs and deliver reporting that supports their goals

• Systems evaluation: Assess the data capabilities of existing and new CS tools, and make recommendations on how to optimise our systems stack for better reporting outcomes

• Process documentation: Document data structures, reporting methodologies, and system configurations to ensure institutional knowledge is retained and accessible across the team

 What You Bring to the Table

• 5-8 years of experience in a data analyst, business intelligence, or systems analyst role, ideally within a customer support or operations environment

• Hands-on experience with Zendesk administration and configuration, including views, fields, triggers, and reporting, as well as using Zendesk Analytics to build reports and dashboards

• Fluency in SQL and experience working with data and BI tools such as Omni, Metabase, or similar

• Strong analytical thinking with the ability to turn complex datasets into clear, actionable insights

• Experience building and maintaining dashboards and reports for non-technical stakeholders

• Deep understanding of data hygiene principles and how system configuration impacts data quality

• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to present data findings clearly to stakeholders at all levels

• Collaborative mindset with experience working cross-functionally across teams such as Operations, Product, and Engineering

 The Ideal Candidate Will Also Have

• Experience working with AI chatbot or conversational analytics platforms

• Familiarity with other CS tools such as Intercom, Guru, or Rippit (formerly known as MaestroQA)

• Experience working in a high-growth SaaS or fintech environment

• Background in supporting data-driven workforce planning or CS strategy initiatives

 The total rewards package at Mercury includes base salary, equity (stock options/RSUs), and benefits.

 Our salary and equity ranges are highly competitive within the SaaS and fintech industry and are updated regularly using the most reliable compensation survey data for our industry. New hire offers are made based on a candidate’s experience, expertise, geographic location, and internal pay equity relative to peers.

 Our target new hire base salary ranges for this role are the following:

title: Counsel, Product & Regulatory - Payments & AML
description:
Headquarters: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States

 In 1905, chief engineer John Stevens inherited one of the most ambitious infrastructure projects in history: the Panama Canal.

 The challenge wasn’t digging a ditch between two oceans. It was figuring out how to move ships safely through a system of locks, gates, reservoirs, and changing conditions without bringing global commerce to a halt.

 The solution wasn’t to stop movement. It was to create a framework that allowed movement at scale.

 Modern financial infrastructure presents a similar challenge. Payment systems, banking products, compliance obligations, and regulatory frameworks all exist for a reason. The goal isn’t to eliminate complexity. It’s to build systems that allow innovation, growth, and customer value within it.

 Who we are

 Since 2019, Mercury has been on a mission to reinvent banking‡ for the modern age. We blend elegant design and cutting-edge technology to offer checking and savings accounts, debit cards, payment services, credit products, cash management tools, and sophisticated analytics. Everything we build reflects our belief that financial products should be thoughtfully crafted, fast, transparent, and genuinely enjoyable to use.

 As we continue expanding and iterating on our product offerings and as we work to build a nationally chartered bank, we’re looking for a Counsel, Product & Regulatory (Payments & AML) to help us navigate increasingly complex questions at the intersection of product, regulation, and financial infrastructure.

 About the team

 Our Product & Regulatory Legal team operates like the rest of Mercury: with urgency, curiosity, and a bias toward action.

 We embed with product teams from early ideation through launch, working alongside engineers, designers, compliance partners, operations teams, and risk stakeholders to get products right. We move fast, we take ownership, and we don’t wait to be asked. If something needs figuring out, we’re up to the task.

 We are not a team that sits on the sidelines reviewing finished proposals. We work alongside our partners to identify risks, unlock opportunities, and find practical paths forward. We care deeply about good judgment, strong relationships, and building frameworks that scale.

 What you’ll do

• Advise on payments products and infrastructure. You’ll support a broad portfolio of payments-related initiatives across Mercury. You’ll advise on matters involving payment rails, product launches, operational incidents, partner relationships, and customer-facing experiences. You’ll help product teams navigate regulatory complexity while continuing to build exceptional products.

• Partner across the company. This role sits at the intersection of Product, Compliance, Risk, Engineering, Operations, Partnerships, and Legal. You’ll build trusted relationships across these functions and bring legal perspective into conversations early, not as a checkpoint, but as a low-ego, high-ownership thought partner.

• Help launch new capabilities. Mercury is continuing to expand its product offerings while building a nationally chartered bank. You’ll support new payment capabilities (like Zelle) from early exploration through launch, helping teams identify risks, evaluate options, and make sound decisions in ambiguous environments.

• Support financial crimes initiatives. You’ll work closely with Mercury’s AML Advisory, Sanctions, Compliance, and Risk teams on matters involving financial crimes compliance. You’ll help interpret requirements, evaluate new initiatives, and develop practical guidance that enables teams to move efficiently while maintaining an appropriate risk posture.

• Build scalable guidance. The best legal advice solves more than the question in front of you. You’ll help create frameworks and guidance that improve consistency, reduce friction, and allow the organization to make better decisions over time.

• Use AI intentionally. Bring a working knowledge of AI tools in legal workflows and a genuine interest in finding new ways to drive efficiency. We’re building a legal team that works smarter, not just harder.

• Stay curious and adaptable. The regulatory and product landscape continues to evolve quickly. New payment rails emerge. Regulatory expectations shift. Business priorities change. You’ll embrace that complexity and continue learning alongside it.

 What you should have

• 4+ years of legal experience.

• Active license to practice law in at least one U.S. jurisdiction.

• Experience supporting fintechs, banks, payment companies, sponsor-bank programs, payment networks, BaaS providers, or regulators with substantial payments- or AML-related exposure.

• Strong working knowledge of payments-related regulatory frameworks, and an interest in emerging areas like stablecoins.

• Familiarity with BSA/AML and sanctions requirements.

• Exceptional communication skills. You know your audience and tailor accordingly.

• Strong judgment and comfort operating in ambiguous environments.

• A proactive sense of ownership. You’re comfortable saying, “I don’t know yet, but I’ll find out.”

• Genuine curiosity about financial products, financial infrastructure, and the evolving regulatory landscape.

• Strong working knowledge of AI use cases within legal roles and/or financial services generally and genuine interest in using AI to drive efficiency in your work.

 What will make you successful here

 Mercury is a place where lawyers are expected to have a point of view. Not just about what a regulation requires, but about how a product can meet that requirement in a way that’s thoughtful, scalable, and good for customers.

 The people who thrive on this team treat ambiguity as an invitation rather than a reason to pause. They read a regulation and think about what it permits, not just what it prohibits. They understand that legal advice is most valuable when it helps the business make a decision, not when it simply identifies a risk.

 You’ll also spend a meaningful amount of your time on work that may not look like traditional legal practice: helping scope cross-functional projects, pressure-testing product designs, navigating operational questions, and building processes alongside compliance and operational partners.

 If you’re energized by that kind of work, and if you measure your impact by whether the product, process, or customer experience got better—not just whether the memo was technically correct—you’ll do well here.

 Why this role

 This is an opportunity to join Mercury during a uniquely consequential period of growth.

 You’ll help support existing products while contributing to the development of new capabilities as Mercury builds a nationally chartered bank. You’ll work alongside experienced legal, compliance, product, and banking professionals, gain exposure to a wide range of regulatory and product questions, and have meaningful ownership early in your career. You’ll also help shape how Mercury approaches payments and financial crimes legal support for years to come.

 The total rewards package at Mercury includes base salary, equity (stock options), and benefits.

 Our salary and equity ranges are highly competitive within the SaaS and fintech industry and are updated regularly using the most reliable compensation survey data for our industry. New hire offers are made based on a candidate’s experience, expertise, geographic location, and internal pay equity relative to peers.

 Our target new hire base salary ranges for this role are the following:

• US employees in New York City, Los Angeles, Seattle, or the San Francisco Bay Area: $186,400 - $209,700

• US employees outside of the New York City, Los Angeles, Seattle, or the San Francisco Bay Area: $167,800 - $188,700

• Canadian employees (any location): $176,100 - $198,200 CAD

title: Principal Product Engineer - Custom Layout & Virtuoso Applications
description:
At Cadence, we hire and develop leaders and innovators who want to make an impact on the world of technology.

Cadence is a pivotal leader in electronic design, building upon more than 30 years of computational software expertise. The company applies its underlying Intelligent System Design strategy to deliver software, hardware and IP that turn design concepts into reality.

Cadence customers are the world's most innovative companies, delivering extraordinary electronic products from chips to boards to systems for the most dynamic market applications including consumer, hyperscale computing, 5G communications, automotive, aerospace, industrial and health.

At Cadence, we hire and develop leaders and innovators who want to make an impact on the world of technology.

Job Title: Principal Product Engineer - Custom Layout & Virtuoso Applications

Location: Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Reports to: Product Engineering Group Director

Job Overview:

The Principal Product Engineer - Custom Layout & Virtuoso Applications plays a central role in bridging Cadence's world-class electronic design tools with the needs of our most strategic customers. Working at the intersection of customer success, R&D, and product development, this role shapes how customers adopt and succeed with the Virtuoso platform for custom analog and FinFet-based design.

The successful candidate will drive both technical depth and cross-functional collaboration - translating real-world customer challenges into product improvements that benefit the broader Cadence ecosystem.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Engage directly with customers to understand their custom analog design and layout requirements - with particular focus on FinFet-based flows within the Virtuoso platform - and translate those needs into actionable product guidance.
  • Attend and contribute to technical review meetings (at Cadence offices and customer sites), delivering presentations and providing expert commentary on product capabilities and roadmap alignment.
  • Conduct regular on-site customer visits to deliver education and enablement sessions on the Virtuoso cockpit, debug tool-related issues in context, and capture structured feedback for R&D - filing Change Correction Requests (CCRs) where required.
  • Develop and deliver demonstrations and Rapid Adoption Kits (RAKs) that enable the sales team to effectively position Virtuoso products - including delivering training sessions directly to sales and pre-sales teams.
  • Build SKILL-based utilities to address specific customer requirements not covered by standard Virtuoso functionality, including defining and executing validation plans before customer delivery.
  • Use the Virtuoso platform to create test schematics and layouts, validate newly implemented features, and provide structured feedback to R&D - driving necessary changes through to resolution.
  • Author Product Requirement Specifications (PRS) to formalise customer-driven R&D priorities, working within cross-functional teams (CFTs) to achieve alignment across engineering, product, and commercial stakeholders.
  • Partner with the Product Validation (PV) team to ensure rigorous validation of customer flows, contributing flow tests for regression testing and quality assurance.
  • Collaborate with Technical Publications to ensure documentation is accurate, accessible, and highlights features of strategic relevance to customers.
  • Work with marketing to inform tool positioning and licensing strategy based on direct customer feedback and field observations.

Job Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronic Engineering, or a related field - or equivalent professional experience.
  • 5-8 years of experience in the electronic design automation (EDA) industry or a closely related technical field.
  • Demonstrated experience in custom analog layout, including a strong understanding of the challenges specific to analog layout workflows.
  • Hands-on experience with the Virtuoso Layout Suite for connectivity-driven layout.
  • Familiarity with the SKILL programming language, with the ability to write functional utilities independently.

Additional Skills/Preferences:

  • Experience with FinFet layout techniques and multi-patterning methodologies.
  • Experience with the Virtuoso Analog Design Environment (ADE).
  • Knowledge of Innovus and Open-Access frameworks.
  • Proficiency in scripting languages such as TCL or Perl.
  • Experience working in a customer-facing or field applications engineering role.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex technical content to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Additional Information:

This role sits within Cadence's Product Engineering organisation and works at the confluence of R&D, sales, and customer success. Key internal stakeholders include R&D teams, Product Validation, Technical Publications, and Marketing. Externally, you will engage regularly with some of Cadence's most technically sophisticated customers across the semiconductor and systems design space.

Primary tools and platforms include Virtuoso Layout Suite, Virtuoso ADE, the SKILL programming language, and internal Cadence product lifecycle and defect tracking systems.

Check what we can offer you:

  • Competitive salary
  • 25 days holiday per year
  • Private Medical and Dental plans, Income Protection and Life Insurance
  • Group Personal Pension Plan
  • Cycle to work scheme and gym subsidy
  • 5 days paid time to volunteer to give back to our communities
  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan
  • The opportunity to work for a Great Place to Work© & Fortune 100 organization

Cadence is committed to equal employment opportunity and employment equity throughout all levels of the organization. We strive to attract a qualified and diverse candidate pool and encourage diversity and inclusion in the workplace.

Travel: Occasional travel to customer sites and Cadence offices is expected (estimated < 10% of time). Most travel will be domestic, with some international travel possible depending on customer base.

We're doing work that matters. Help us solve what others can't.

title: Machine Learning Engineer 3D Geometry/ Multi-Modal
description:
Job Requisition ID #

26WD100236

Job Description

Position Overview
The work we do at Autodesk touches nearly every person on the planet. By creating software tools for making buildings, machines, and even the latest movies, we influence and empower some of the most creative people in the world.

As a Machine Learning Engineer at Autodesk Research, you will work side-by-side with researchers and engineers to build and enable ML-powered capabilities in Autodesk products. You are an ML engineer with strong software engineering skills who is passionate about solving problems and building things, and excited to collaborate with AI researchers to implement generative AI features. You will operate in a fast-moving, research-driven environment where problems are often not fully defined, requiring strong problem framing and rapid iteration.

The team work in a hybrid working model from our offices in London.

Responsibilities

  • Collaborate on projects at the intersection of research and product with a diverse, global team
  • Build and iterate on ML pipelines, prototypes, and evaluation workflows, enabling rapid deployment and testing of experimental models
  • Work with complex datasets and representations for model training, evaluation, and analysis
  • Analyze errors and provide solutions to problems
  • Present results to collaborators and leadership

Minimum Qualifications

  • BSc or MSc in Computer Science, or equivalent industry experience
  • 3+ years of machine learning experience
  • Experience working in research or experimental environments with evolving requirements
  • Proficiency with modern deep learning libraries and frameworks (PyTorch, HuggingFace)
  • Experience with computational geometry and 3D data (e.g., meshes, B-Rep models)
  • Experience working with diverse data representations, including 2D and 3D geometry
  • Experience with version control, reproducibility, and deploying machine learning models
  • Experience using modern AI/GenAI tools in development or experimentation workflows
  • Excellent written documentation skills

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced degree (MSc/PhD) in Machine Learning, Computer Science, or related field
  • Experience scaling machine learning training and data pipelines (e.g., using Ray or similar frameworks)
  • Experience with cloud services and architectures (e.g. AWS, Azure)
  • Experience with LLMs or generative AI systems (fine-tuning, prompting, evaluation)
  • Knowledge of the design, manufacturing, AEC, or media & entertainment industries
  • Experience with Autodesk or similar products (CAD, CAE, CAM, etc.)

Learn More

About Autodesk

Welcome to Autodesk! Amazing things are created every day with our software - from the greenest buildings and cleanest cars to the smartest factories and biggest hit movies. We help innovators turn their ideas into reality, transforming not only how things are made, but what can be made.

We take great pride in our culture here at Autodesk - it's at the core of everything we do. Our culture guides the way we work and treat each other, informs how we connect with customers and partners, and defines how we show up in the world.

When you're an Autodesker, you can do meaningful work that helps build a better world designed and made for all. Ready to shape the world and your future? Join us!

Salary transparency
Salary is one part of Autodesk's competitive compensation package. Offers are based on the candidate's experience and geographic location. In addition to base salaries, our compensation package may include annual cash bonuses, commissions for sales roles, stock grants, and a comprehensive benefits package.

Belonging
We take pride in cultivating a culture of belonging where everyone can thrive. Learn more here: https://www.autodesk.com/company/global-belonging

Are you an existing contractor or consultant with Autodesk?

Please search for open jobs and apply internally (not on this external site).

title: Director of ML Engineering, Conversation Product Area
description:
The Personalization team makes deciding what to play next easier and more enjoyable for every listener. From Blend to Discover Weekly, we're behind some of Spotify's most-loved features. We built them by understanding the world of music and podcasts better than anyone else. Join us and you'll keep millions of users listening by making great recommendations to each and every one of them.
Spotify's Personalization mission (PZN) is building the single intelligence layer that powers how hundreds of millions of people discover and experience audio. One agent, one reasoning engine, and one taste model, moving to a unified single stack. 
We're looking for a Director of Engineering to lead the Conversation Product Area. The Conversation Product Area is the technical center of gravity for the shift to one Agent, building the shared Agent Engine harness and the evaluation infrastructure that supports it. The Product Area also owns the Search Brain (intent routing and search-driven conversation) the intent-detection and prompt-suggestion platform behind our agentic consumer features like Chat and AI DJ, and the Speak Platform, Spotify's first-party voice team, which spans applied research, production infrastructure, and the character/brand decisions behind every voice Spotify users hear. This is the engineering org where architecture decisions get made that power every agentic surface at the company.
You'll be working with many of Spotify's senior architects, with product leadership in the consumer AI space, and with cross functional partners. The team needs a leader who is as comfortable making critical architectural calls as they are managing the people making them.

title: DevOps Engineer IV (Obs)
description:
Headquarters: India (remote)

 Role Purpose

 As a DevOps Engineer IV at Jumio, you are expected to be strong in both the “Dev” and “Ops” aspects of DevOps. We are seeking someone with a deep understanding of systems architecture and core computer science concepts, who can reason about system behavior rather than simply working with current toolsets.

 This is a high-bar role with significant rewards. As one of our hires in our Bengaluru office, you will help shape the team and culture, collaborate with energetic peers who will challenge and inspire you, and gain considerable international exposure with opportunities for cross-departmental impact.

 Role Value

 This role is an individual contributor position within the Production team, with some focus on observability to improve reliability of our platform and boost engineer productivity. You will mentor junior engineers and drive collaborative projects across teams.

 Responsibilities

• Deploy, manage, and administer web services in public cloud environments.

• Design and develop solutions for secure, highly available, performant, and scalable services in elastic environments.

• Own all operational aspects of web services: automation, monitoring, alerting, reliability, and performance.

• Innovate solutions to operational challenges with a direct business impact.

• Drive resolution and communication during production-impacting incidents.

• Lead technical projects and ensure project-level deliveries.

• Collaborate effectively with engineering and business teams across continents.

 Experience & Qualifications

• Bachelor’s or advanced degree in Computer Science or a related field.

• 8+ years of professional DevOps / Infrastructure management experience, with 5+ years in AWS .

• Strong foundation in operating systems, networking, distributed systems, and systems architecture.

• Proven track record of leading critical DevOps projects.

• Hands-on expertise with AWS services, orchestration (ECS, EKS), and infrastructure management.

• Proficiency with observability concepts (logs, metrics, tracing)

• Experience with SaaS observability platforms (eg Datadog, NewRelic, Honeycomb, Dynatrace…) and building in-house solutions (ELK stack, Prometheus, Grafana stack…)

• Strong scripting and automation skills (Python, Bash).

• Solid experience with Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, CloudFormation, Packer) and containerization (Docker, Kubernetes).

• Strong debugging, troubleshooting, and problem-solving abilities.

• Broad exposure to cloud-hosted applications, virtualization platforms, relational/non-relational databases, reverse proxies, and orchestration platforms.

• Excellent communication, collaboration, and stakeholder management skills.

• Demonstrated curiosity, continuous learning, and drive to raise the technical bar.

 Nice to Have

• Prior experience as a senior developer or application architect.

• Experience in cloud cost optimization and exposure to FinOps concepts (cost allocation, unit economics…)

• Experience working in compliance-regulated environments (PCI DSS, ISO 27000, HIPAA, SOC 2, GDPR).

 Key Characteristics & Attitudes

 We hire for attitude as much as skill. Attributes highly valued across Jumio include:

• Friendly and supportive

• Adaptable and flexible

• Articulate and persuasive

• High IQ and EQ

 Jumio Values

• Curious and coachable

• Commercially aware

• Resilient and tenacious

• Big-picture thinking with attention to detail

 IDEAL Values: Integrity, Diversity, Empowerment, Accountability, Leading Innovation

 About Jumio

 Jumio is the leading provider of online identity verification, eKYC, and AML solutions . With a global footprint, we are expanding to meet strong client demand across industries such as Financial Services, Travel, Sharing Economy, Fintech, Gaming, and more.

 Equal Opportunities

 Jumio is a collaboration of people with diverse ideas, strengths, interests, and cultures. We welcome applications from colleagues of all backgrounds and statuses .
 Jumio Values:

 IDEAL: Integrity, Diversity, Empowerment, Accountability, Leading Innovation

 Equal Opportunities :

 Jumio is a collaboration of people with different ideas, strengths, interests and cultures. We welcome applications and colleagues from all backgrounds and of all statuses.

 About Jumio:

 Jumio is a B2B technology company dedicated to eradicating online identity fraud, money laundering and other financial crimes to help make the internet safer. We leverage AI, biometrics, machine learning, liveness detection and automation to create solutions that are trusted by leading brands worldwide and respected by industry thought leaders.

 Jumio is the leading provider of online identity verification, eKYC and AML solutions. With a global footprint, we’re expanding the team to meet strong client demand across a range of industries including Financial Services, Travel, Sharing Economy, Fintech, Gaming, and others.

 Applicant Data Privacy

 We will only use your personal information in connection with Jumio’s application, recruitment, and hiring processes, as described in Jumio’s Applicant Privacy Notice. If you have any questions or comments, please send an email to privacy@jumio.com .
